description: Single source of truth for Beam performance budgets. Consumed by the CI gate (swift run perf-gate) and the in-app perf HUD. 'budget' is the design target; 'gate' is the CI failure threshold. tier 'pr' = deterministic or dev-machine-runnable; 'rig' = requires the dedicated two-machine LAN rig; 'weekly' = long-running.

conventions.latency: All timing metrics report p50/p95/p99/p99.9/max. Budgets specify which statistic they constrain. Never gate on the mean.
conventions.baselineComparison: In addition to absolute gates, any metric regressing >5% versus the baseline commit is reported; >15% fails.
conventions.e2eMethod: Clock-sync-free round-trip decomposition: E2E = RTT/2 + d_remote. See PLAN.md 3.1.
conventions.clockDomain: t0 is NSEvent.timestamp (IOHID, mach/systemUptime domain); present times are CAMetalDrawable.presentedTime / MTLCommandBuffer gpu times, same domain. Never compare timestamps across machines.
conventions.cameraOffsetNote: Constant software-presented -> photon offset, derived once per rig by 240fps camera per PLAN.md 3.1. null = not yet calibrated; photon metrics cannot be claimed until set.

L0_physical_floor.note: Calibration only, never a gate. Measured per rig so higher layers report overhead above the wire.

launch_to_first_frame_ms.note: Process exec (kinfo_proc start time) to first drawable presented. Includes runtime Metal shader compile — deliberately, so it is owned by a budget.

launch_to_typeable_ms.note: First frame presented with key window + first responder accepting keystrokes. RE-SPECIFIED Phase 1 (PLAN.md 5.3): this now means typeable IN A DOCUMENT, not on a peer list — a strictly stronger claim on the same instrument. Beam launches into an EMPTY untitled buffer for exactly this reason: restoring a file would put disk I/O inside a launch budget in exchange for nothing the user asked for. `beam <path>` opens a path; the budget is unchanged and was not touched after seeing a number.

launch_to_peers_visible_ms.note: App launch (process exec) to a peer PRESENTED on the glass. RE-SPECIFIED Phase 1 (PLAN.md 5.3): the launch screen is no longer the peer list, so the mark moved from a roster row to the peer's CHIP IN THE STATUS LINE — the presence readout that is now visible from inside the document at all times, which the roster never was. The instrument is unchanged (CAMetalDrawable.presentedTime, not a model callback) and 5.2's fade floor still applies, so the frame that claims the number is one a human could read. Budget unchanged; re-specified before any number moved.
launch_to_peers_visible_ms.method: beam --bench-join (guest, cold-launched into a network that already has a peer)

linked_dylibs.note: otool -L on the release binary. Catches accidental dependency creep.

keystroke_to_commit_p50_ms.note: NSEvent.timestamp -> command buffer committed + present() called. The pure software path; refresh-rate independent.

keystroke_to_presented_60hz_p50_ms.note: NSEvent.timestamp -> CAMetalDrawable.presentedTime, 60 Hz dev panel, MEASURED FLOOR of the naive one-shot present path (2026-08-30: phase-uniform distribution = uniform(0..16.7) + ~17 ms constant — an idle window's present misses the imminent vsync and lands a full frame later; displaySyncEnabled=false shows the non-vsync machinery is ~5 ms). Holding the line here; halving it via present-path engineering (display-link-aligned presents, presentsWithTransaction, direct-to-display — camera-decided) is Phase 1's headline objective with the aspirational numbers on the 120hz/photon rows. See PLAN.md 5-L2.

keystroke_to_photon_120hz_p50_ms.note: Camera-verified: presented_120hz + conventions.cameraOffsetMs. Cannot be reported until cameraOffsetMs is calibrated.

keystroke_to_presented_60hz_min_ms.note: PIPELINE DEPTH: the luckiest keystroke's latency — how fast the present path can possibly show a glyph. Validated 17.0 ms 2026-08-30 (a whole extra frame of pipeline); the Phase-1 present-path work is judged by driving this down, and this gate stops it creeping up meanwhile.

presented_spread_p99_minus_p50_60hz_ms.note: JITTER as a first-class metric: the tail is the UX. p99 minus p50 of keystroke->presented. Validated 7.96 ms with the hybrid render loop (was 13.0 on the naive path).

burst_125hz_presented_p99_60hz_ms.note: 150 keystrokes at 8 ms — faster than key repeat. Accounting is worst-case-honest: each coalesced frame records its OLDEST keystroke. Validated 48.6 ms with in-frame coalescing (no drops, no starvation; naive per-key presents starved the drawable queue). Scales down with pipeline depth — the same Phase-1 work pays here.

first_keystroke_after_idle_p50_ms.note: The cold-pipeline tax: single keystrokes after 2 s of quiet — the keystroke users actually feel. Includes drop-recovery: the first present after idle can be dropped; wake-double-present bounds recovery at ~1 tick. Validated 59.5 ms (deadline-driven recovery measured 91.8; broken recovery measured 1735). Improvement path: longer warm window, second immediate present, pipeline-depth work.

first_keystroke_after_idle_max_ms.note: See p50 row. Validated max 62.9 ms. A multi-hundred-ms max means drop recovery is broken.

tab_switch_to_presented_60hz_p99_ms.note: Key event -> the frame carrying the newly-fronted document PRESENTED. Deliberately the SAME budget as a keystroke: a command IS input, and a tab strip that is slower than typing is a tab strip people stop using. Switching must not re-read, re-scan or re-lex anything — each document keeps its own buffer, line index, undo stack and token cache, so a switch is a pointer change and a repaint. BEAM_SABOTAGE_KEY_DELAY_MS reddens it, since it shares the keystroke path.

zoom_step_to_presented_60hz_p99_ms.note: One zoom step (⌘+ / ⌘− / ⌘0) -> the frame at the new size PRESENTED. Deliberately the SAME budget as a keystroke and as a tab switch, for the same reason (PLAN.md 5.4): a command IS input, and a zoom that is slower than typing is a zoom people stop using. It is the most expensive command Beam has — the whole glyph atlas is re-rasterized (95 ASCII glyphs plus every shape glyph), every demand-filled GlyphCache slot is evicted, every layout constant re-derives, the scroll offset is rescaled and the tracking areas are rebuilt — so this row exists to say that being expensive is not the same as being allowed to be slow. Budget written before the first measurement, per PLAN.md 3; BEAM_SABOTAGE_ZOOM_DELAY_MS proves it can go red.

keystroke_to_commit_zoomed_p99_ms.note: The same paced typing pass as keystroke_to_commit_p99_ms, run after zooming two steps in. Deliberately the SAME budget as the unzoomed row: point size must not be visible in typing latency. A bigger font means a bigger atlas texture and more pixels per glyph, but the commit path builds the same instances either way, so a regression here means the zoom left something per-keystroke behind it — a stale cache consulted on every character, or a metric being recomputed rather than read.

open_1mb_file_to_first_paint_ms.note: Choosing a file in the open overlay -> the frame carrying its first line PRESENTED. Read + line-index scan + one frame; the read and the scan are the part that is ours, and the budget leaves a frame of quantization on top of them. A file view whose first paint is felt is a file view nobody opens twice.

keystroke_to_commit_1mb_doc_p99_ms.note: The same paced typing pass, into a loaded 1 MB document instead of an empty one. Deliberately the SAME budget as the empty-document row: document size must not be visible in typing latency, which is exactly the claim the raw-coordinate line index in PLAN.md 5.3 exists to make true. A regression here means the line index started doing O(lines) work per keystroke.

scroll_wheel_to_presented_60hz_p99_ms.note: Scroll event timestamp -> the frame carrying the new scroll offset PRESENTED. Same budget as the keystroke row because it is the same present path; scrolling is input, and an editor that types in 26 ms and scrolls in 60 has not understood what it is selling.

scroll_dropped_frames_pct.note: Percentage of display-link ticks during a sustained full-speed scroll that produced no presented frame. Design target is ZERO: a dropped frame mid-scroll is the single most-felt defect in a text editor, and the hybrid loop already coalesces to the tick, so any drop here is real work overrunning a frame.

selection_drag_to_presented_60hz_p99_ms.note: mouseDragged timestamp -> the frame carrying the extended selection PRESENTED. Selection is drawn as fills written before the text in the same buffer, so this should be indistinguishable from the keystroke path; the row exists so that stops being an assumption.

overlay_keystroke_to_commit_p99_ms.note: A keystroke in the open overlay's query -> commit, with a realistic candidate set. This is the file-tree keystroke cost: filtering runs on the keystroke path (there is nowhere else to put it), so it is budgeted rather than trusted. Rebuilding the whole candidate list per keystroke is what this catches.

atlas_miss_rasterize_p99_us.note: CoreText rasterization of one scalar the atlas does not have, into one cell, including the font-cascade lookup. Paid once per distinct character per session, ON the keystroke path the first time it is seen — a one-shot spike rather than a per-frame tax, but a spike inside the commit budget is still a spike. BEAM_SABOTAGE_ATLAS_MISS_US proves it can go red.

undo_10k_depth_p99_us.note: One undo step with 10k records on the stack. Depth must not be visible in the cost of a step; a regression here means undo started scanning its own history.

syntax_highlight_line_p99_us.note: Lexing one line of real source into cached token spans. Bounded by the VIEWPORT, never by the file: an edit marks lines dirty and the frame lexes only the dirty lines that are visible. The enforcement that actually matters is that keystroke_to_commit, the presented rows and malloc_bytes_per_keystroke do not move — PLAN.md 6 reverts highlighting if they do, and 5.3 does not soften that.

draw_calls_per_frame.note: Phases 0-2 measured 1. Phase 1 spends the budget on the thing it was reserved for: the document plane carries the sub-cell SCROLL offset in its origin and a scissor rect, and the chrome plane does not, so they cannot share a draw. Pixel-quantized scrolling instead of cell-quantized is the sharpest single TUI/GUI decision in 5.3 and this is its whole cost. A third plane would breach the budget, which is the point of having one.

malloc_bytes_per_keystroke.note: Net malloc bytes per keystroke over the paced window (malloc_zone_statistics delta / n). Design target stays 0 net steady-state; measured ~-22 bytes with direct-to-MTLBuffer instance building. Ratchet the budget down as it proves stable.

L3_transport.note: Loopback numbers are a software floor, not LAN numbers (PLAN.md 3.1). LAN overhead rows gate on the rig against the measured L0 floor.

nagle_spikes_in_10k_msgs.note: Samples >35 ms in an otherwise sub-ms distribution = Nagle/delayed-ACK interaction. noDelay regression detector; BEAM_SABOTAGE_NO_NODELAY=1 proves it can go red.

lan_tcp_echo_overhead_above_floor_p99_ms.method: bench-tcp-echo on rig, minus L0 wired floor

L4_crdt_yrs.note: yrs must reproduce the predecessor's measured Yjs costs (encode 30us/18B, apply 11us) within these budgets before it is committed to.

browse_to_peer_found_ms.note: NWBrowser start -> advertised Bonjour peer in results. Requires Local Network TCC grant; a denial must surface as an explicit error, never a silent miss.

join_to_editing_5mb_workspace_ms.note: Join gesture confirmed -> full snapshot applied and guest can type. Wired.

join_gesture_to_code_visible_ms.note: THE CONNECTION MOMENT. Gesture -> the 6-digit verification code is PRESENTED on BOTH screens (max of the two presentedTimes, single machine = one clock domain). This is the number the 'feels instant' claim rests on: everything before a human has to decide anything. RE-SPECIFIED Phase 1 (PLAN.md 5.3): the launch screen is a document now, so reaching the peer list is a keypress and THE GESTURE IS STILL THE PEER'S NUMBER (or a click on its row) — the mark starts there, not at the keypress that opened the list. Opening a list is navigation and the time a human spends reading it is not ours to budget, which is the same argument the auto-confirm below already makes. Budget unchanged; re-specified before any number moved.

join_confirm_to_editing_ms.note: Host presses return -> guest's editor surface is presented and accepting keystrokes. The half of the join a human is not in.

join_gesture_to_first_shared_keystroke_m.note: HEADLINE, PLAN.md 6 Phase 2 exit: gesture -> ECDH handshake -> code shown+auto-confirmed -> encrypted session -> guest's first keystroke PRESENTED on the host's screen. Auto-confirm means human think time is excluded (deliberately: it is not ours to budget); every millisecond of machine time is included. Discovery time sits in L1.launch_to_peers_visible_ms, so discovery+join < 1 s is these two rows added.

handshake_crypto_cpu_ms.note: X25519 key agreement + HKDF derivation of the two directional session keys and the SAS, measured on the join hot path. Cheap by design; gated so a heavier scheme cannot slip onto the gesture path unnoticed.

L6_end_to_end.note: Wired/Wi-Fi rows need the two-machine rig. The loopback row below is a SOFTWARE FLOOR (PLAN.md 3.1) — it is not a LAN number and never substitutes for one; it exists so a regression in the send/receive/apply/render path is caught on every PR instead of only on the rig.

keystroke_to_remote_present_loopback_p99.note: Guest keystroke t0 -> the frame containing it PRESENTED on the host, both processes on one machine (one mach clock domain, so this is a direct subtraction; the cross-machine rig rows use RTT decomposition instead). Floored by the local present path (60 Hz presented p99 33.8 ms), so this budget is that plus transport+apply headroom — it gates the DELTA, not the frame quantization.

bytes_per_keystroke_on_wire.note: Bytes actually written to the socket per keystroke, ciphertext included (4 B length + AEAD tag + payload). Phase 2 sends a 2-byte op; Phase 3 replaces it with a yrs update and must stay under the same budget.

relay_rtt_under_host_stall_max_ms.note: Guest RTT-probes host relay while host main thread busy-loops 200 ms. Flat only because relay runs on its own thread/event loop — this is that architecture's regression detector (predecessor: <=1.3 ms max).

idle_cpu_connected_pct_core.note: Most collab/Electron apps idle at 3-8%. Deliberate differentiator and battery feature. Measured on loopback from Phase 2: an established encrypted session, both peers quiet, worst of the two processes. This is the gate that makes 'live RTT in the UI' honest — a per-second repaint to animate a number would show up here, which is exactly why the roster repaints only when a displayed value actually changes and why nothing in Beam blinks.

caret_blink_cpu_pct_core.note: CPU while the caret is pulsing and nothing else is happening (PLAN.md 5.5). A blink is frames, and frames are the price — what keeps the price bounded is that the animation is FINITE (it stops after GridView.caretBlinkWindow) and that the loop presents only when the curve has actually moved. The curve is flat for about 89% of its period, so a 60 Hz display link produces roughly 7 presents a second rather than 60. Most editors idle at 3-8% doing nothing at all; this is the number that keeps an animated caret honest in a product whose idle loop is a feature.

idle_cpu_foreground_alone_pct_core.note: Foreground, no session, no input: event-driven rendering with the display link paused must idle at ~0. BEAM_SABOTAGE_IDLE_SPIN=1 proves the gate can go red. The bench measures its window AFTER the caret has stopped pulsing (PLAN.md 5.5), so this row still means what it has always meant: display link paused, nothing moving. The caret's own cost is gated separately by caret_blink_cpu_pct_core rather than folded in here. RE-SPECIFIED Phase 1 (PLAN.md 5.3): the bench also starts DISCOVERY, because Beam no longer idles on a roster whose whole job was discovery — it idles on a document with discovery running behind it, and a bench that did not start it would be measuring a state the product never has. This is a strictly harder measurement on the same instrument; the budget is unchanged and was not touched after seeing a number. Measured 0.085% without discovery and 0.101-0.118% with, so discovery in the background costs about 0.02-0.03% of a core.

rss_with_1mb_file_mb.note: RSS with a 1 MB document open and scrolled through end to end, so the per-line token cache and the demand-filled atlas slots are populated. The document itself is 1 MB and its line index a further ~120 KB; anything beyond that headroom is a per-line cache that is not bounded.

packaged_launch_ok.note: scripts/verify_app.sh executes the packaged binary DIRECTLY and requires the BEAM_LAUNCH_OK sentinel on stderr + exit 0. The predecessor shipped a silently-broken .app for weeks; this is the never-again gate.
